text:
sam: Heads-up — cloud negotiation call tomorrow. We need stronger protections for reserved GPU commitments across regions. TL;DR: ask for preemption insurance + region-fallback credits.

maria: Agree. Past EDPs left us exposed when a region ran out. Need explicit capacity SLO or financial remediation.

alex: Do we have numbers for impact? e.g., how many vGPU-hours per month we had bounce last quarter due to regional shortages?

sam: Roughly 140k GPU-hours shifted between regions in Q4, cost spike ~12%. Not huge but repeated thrash is bad for latency SLOs.

emma: For negotiation, two asks: 1) guaranteed baseline capacity per region (min x gpus) or cross-region failover credits; 2) preemption insurance: credits for preemptible interruptions > threshold.

leo: +1. Also ask for metering clarity: timestamps on metering events, SKU mapping when capacity is offloaded to lower-tier instances. We got billed full rate once even though instance was preempted then replaced.

procurement-bot: Suggestion: propose a multi-tier remediation matrix. Example: if monthly capacity shortfall >5% for >48h, vendor issues credits equal to compute-hours lost * committed rate * 1.25.

maria: Love that. Can we get a short clause we can drop into the redline? Something lawyer-friendly but simple.

alex: Draft clause suggestion below — feel free to reuse/edit: 

```
Capacity & Preemption Remediation: Vendor warrants availability of the committed GPU capacity set forth in Schedule A per region. If Vendor fails to provide at least 95% of committed capacity in a single region for more than 48 consecutive hours in a billing month, Vendor shall (a) provide customers the option to (i) credit the customer an amount equal to 1.25x the committed hourly rate for hours of shortfall, or (ii) supply equivalent replacement capacity in a different region within 24 hours and cover cross-region egress at Vendor's expense, and (b) not charge for replacement instances used during remediation.
```

emma: That reads clear. Add a line about metering transparency: vendor must provide event-level metering CSV within 24h of request.

sam: Also request guaranteed notification window: 2hr heads-up before any forced preemption or capacity carve-out affecting >1% of our pool. If they can't, automatic credit applies.

leo: On the financial side, ask for a staircase clause for rampdown of committed units (30/60/90 days notice) rather than immediate penalties on minor misses. We don't want to be locked if demand drops.

procurement-bot: Actionables: 
1) Use Alex's clause in the redline draft for tomorrow.
2) Maria to pull GA metering examples and last quarter shifting numbers.
3) Leo + Finance to craft acceptable staircase (propose 10%/10%/10% over 90 days).
4) Sam to request a 2-hr notification SLA and preemption credits formula.

maria: I'll attach the Q4 report in the doc before the call.

alex: One more: request a single-pane inventory for committed SKUs per region (API access). Saves emails during outages.

emma: +1. API access should be part of the SOW.

sam: Great. I'll push these into the negotiation deck tonight. Thanks team :rocket:

leo: Nice. If they push back on credits, we can trade higher committed volume for stronger remediation terms. Good bargaining chip.

procurement-bot: Noted — tagging vendor-negotiation thread and adding reminder 1h before meeting.

sam: Cool — end of thread.
